L103: # Bench2Drive: Towards Multi-Ability Benchmarking of Closed-Loop End-To-End Autonomous Driving.
L104: ## Description
L105: 
L106: Bench2Drive is a benchmark designed for evaluating end-to-end autonomous driving algorithms in the closed-loop manner. It features:
L107:   * Comprehensive Scenario Coverage: Bench2Drive is designed to test AD systems across 44 interactive scenarios, ensuring a thorough evaluation of an AD system's capability to handle real-world driving challenges.
L108:   * Granular Skill Assessment: By structuring the evaluation across 220 short routes, each focusing on a specific driving scenario, Bench2Drive allows for detailed analysis and comparison of how different AD systems perform on individual tasks.
L109:   * Closed-Loop Evaluation Protocol: Bench2Drive evaluates AD systems in a closed-loop manner, where the AD system's actions directly influence the environment. This setup offers an accurate assessment of AD systems' driving performance.
L110:   * Diverse Large-Scale Official Training Data: Bench2Drive consists of a standardized training set of 10000 fully annotated clips under diverse scenarios, weathers, and towns, ensuring that all AD systems are trained under abundant yet similar conditions, which is crucial for fair algorithm-level comparisons.
L111: Each clip named by: ScenarioName_TownID_RouteID_WeatherID.tar.gz.

L88: ( repo_id: str filename: str subfolder: str | None = None repo_type: str | None = None revision: str | None = None library_name: str | None = None library_version: str | None = None cache_dir: str | pathlib.Path | None = None local_dir: str | pathlib.Path | None = None user_agent: dict | str | None = None force_download: bool = False etag_timeout: float = 10 token: bool | str | None = None local_files_only: bool = False headers: dict[str, str] | None = None endpoint: str | None = None tqdm_class: type[tqdm.std.tqdm] | None = None dry_run: bool = False ) → `str` or 【81†DryRunFileInfo】
L89: Parameters
L90:   * repo_id (`str`) — A user or an organization name and a repo name separated by a `/`.
L91:   * filename (`str`) — The name of the file in the repo.
L92:   * subfolder (`str`, optional) — An optional value corresponding to a folder inside the model repo.
L93:   * repo_type (`str`, optional) — Set to `"dataset"`, `"space"` or `"kernel"` if downloading from a dataset, space or kernel repo, `None` or `"model"` if downloading from a model. Default is `None`.
L94:   * revision (`str`, optional) — An optional Git revision id which can be a branch name, a tag, or a commit hash.
L95:   * library_name (`str`, optional) — The name of the library to which the object corresponds.
L96:   * library_version (`str`, optional) — The version of the library.
L97:   * cache_dir (`str`, `Path`, optional) — Path to the folder where cached files are stored.
L98:   * local_dir (`str` or `Path`, optional) — If provided, the downloaded file will be placed under this directory.
L99:   * user_agent (`dict`, `str`, optional) — The user-agent info in the form of a dictionary or a string.
L100:   * force_download (`bool`, optional, defaults to `False`) — Whether the file should be downloaded even if it already exists in the local cache.
L101:   * etag_timeout (`float`, optional, defaults to `10`) — When fetching ETag, how many seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, which is passed to `httpx2.request`.
L102:   * token (`str`, `bool`, optional) — A token to be used for the download.
L103:     * If `True`, the token is read from the HuggingFace config folder.
L104:     * If a string, it’s used as the authentication token.
L105:   * local_files_only (`bool`, optional, defaults to `False`) — If `True`, avoid downloading the file and return the path to the local cached file if it exists.
L106:   * headers (`dict`, optional) — Additional headers to be sent with the request.
L107:   * endpoint (`str`, optional) — The Hub endpoint to send the request to. Defaults to the value of `HF_ENDPOINT`.
L108:   * tqdm_class (`tqdm`, optional) — If provided, overwrites the default behavior for the progress bar. Passed argument must inherit from `tqdm.auto.tqdm` or at least mimic its behavior. Defaults to the custom HF progress bar that can be disabled by setting `HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS` environment variable.
L109:   * dry_run (`bool`, optional, defaults to `False`) — If `True`, perform a dry run without actually downloading the file. Returns a 【81†DryRunFileInfo】 object containing information about what would be downloaded.

L111: 
L112: `str` or 【81†DryRunFileInfo】
L113: 
L114:   * If `dry_run=False`: Local path of file or if networking is off, last version of file cached on disk.
L115:   * If `dry_run=True`: A 【81†DryRunFileInfo】 object containing download information.

L127: Download a given file if it’s not already present in the local cache.
L128: 
L129: The new cache file layout looks like this:
L130:   * The cache directory contains one subfolder per repo_id (namespaced by repo type)
L131:   * inside each repo folder:
L132:     * refs is a list of the latest known revision => commit_hash pairs
L133:     * blobs contains the actual file blobs (identified by their git-sha or sha256, depending on whether they’re LFS files or not)
L134:     * snapshots contains one subfolder per commit, each “commit” contains the subset of the files that have been resolved at that particular commit. Each filename is a symlink to the blob at that particular commit.
